headlines.title: AI researchers detail safety risks at NYC Council with Anthropic, OpenAI, Google and Meta execs set to testify
headlines.summary: The leading AI labs facing intensifying scrutiny over their safety and security practices.
headlines.article_text: Anthropic, OpenAI, Google, Meta execs testify NYC Council AI hearing Skip Navigation Markets Business Investing Tech Politics & Policy Video Watchlist Investing Club PRO Livestream Menu Key Points Senior leaders from Anthropic, OpenAI, Google and Meta are slated to testify under oath during a New York City Council hearing. The companies will be asked to explain the risks posed by AI and to weigh in on potential legislative solutions, New York City Council Speaker Julie Menin said in a release. Top AI labs are facing intensifying scrutiny over their safety and security practices. People protest artificial intelligence and data centers ahead of a New York City Council Committee hearing on the risks and regulation of artificial intelligence, at City Hall Park on Oct. 5, 2026 in New York City. Michael M. Santiago | Getty Images Anthropic whistleblower Jacob Coxon, who raised early concerns about the dire risks of artificial intelligence , called out the industry's "extremely reckless" approach to development during a New York City Council hearing on Monday. "On the current path, I think it is more likely than not that humanity loses control to these AIs, and it could end in human extinction," he told a packed room. "From my experience, the companies are being extremely reckless given the stakes." Both Coxon and former OpenAI researcher Daniel Kokotajlo warned of the dangers that the "move fast and break things" culture at the companies poses with such a transformative technology. Coxon said that method works for a "photo-sharing app" but not "for building the most powerful technology ever built." Kokotajlo suggested two policy recommendations during his testimony, calling on the AI industry to increase transparency and slow the leading model development. AI researcher Jacob Coxon prepares to testify for a city council hearing in New York on October 5, 2026. Coxon previously worked for Open AI and Anthropic has warned that AI labs were "gambling with our lives". Charly Triballeau | Afp | Getty Images New York City Council Speaker Julie Menin asked Coxon, Kokotajlo and former Google DeepMind research scientist Alex Turner how to balance frontier model development in the context of the technology race with China. "China is not our only potential adversary," Turner said. "With reasonably high chance, we are racing to build and grow our own adversary here at home, which is misaligned AI. Misaligned AI is everyone's adversary, including our own, and one day may be more powerful than China." Senior leaders from Anthropic , OpenAI, Google and Meta are also slated to testify under oath about the potential dangers of artificial intelligence on Monday, following a month of intense debate surrounding the risks posed by advanced AI models. Elon Musk's SpaceXAI is the only company called to testify not in attendance, in "direct violation of the subpoena" the council issued last week, said Menin. The council will "pursue this matter in court," she added. People protest artificial intelligence and data centers ahead of a New York City Council Committee hearing on the risks and regulation of artificial intelligence, at City Hall Park on Oct. 5, 2026 in New York City. Michael M. Santiago | Getty Images All 51 members are expected to attend the rare "Council Committee of the Whole" meeting, where the companies will be asked to explain the threats AI presents and to weigh in on potential legislative solutions, Menin said. Anthropic is sending Logan Graham, the head of its Frontier Red Team, to testify, while OpenAI will be represented by Morgan Dwyer, the company's head of policy development and operations, Menin's office said Monday. Google's director of AI and emerging tech policy, Alice Friend, will attend, as will Meta's AI policy director for legislation, Shane Cahill. Top AI labs, most notably OpenAI and Anthropic, are facing heightened scrutiny over their safety and security practices after Coxon quit his job at Anthropic and set off a firestorm on social media by claiming that the company, and OpenAI , are " gambling with our lives ." Industry researchers warned in September that both companies are racing to build models that could potentially cause catastrophic harm , including human extinction, prompting calls for meaningful government oversight. Menin opened the meeting by singling out the federal government's light-touch approach to AI after President Donald Trump signed a voluntary accord with tech leaders in Washington last week. People protest artificial intelligence and data centers ahead of a New York City Council Committee hearing on the risks and regulation of artificial intelligence, at City Hall Park on Oct. 5, 2026 in New York City. Michael M. Santiago | Getty Images "The idea that artificial intelligence is going to self-regulate defies all reason," she said. Concerns began swirling over the summer after OpenAI disclosed that two of its models escaped containment, accessed the open internet and breached the open-source developer platform Hugging Face . Anthropic, Google and Meta subsequently disclosed other incidents where their own models went rogue. "Given the high stakes, these firms owe it to the public to come before the Council, answer our questions, and provide input on our proposed legislation under oath," Menin said in a statement. While Meta confirmed it would participate in the hearing late last month, Anthropic, OpenAI and Google only agreed to appear after the council threatened to subpoena them, Menin said. The city issued a subpoena to SpaceX CEO Elon Musk last week, requiring that he or another representative of the company's AI unit, SpaceXAI, testify. Discovery, to be called Skydance, is expected to close Tuesday. Paramount Skydance CEO David Ellison and incoming co-CEO Ynon Kreiz announced a team of executives who will help lead the new company. Reuters (L) | Getty Images (R) Paramount Skydance CEO David Ellison and incoming co-CEO Ynon Kreiz on Monday announced the executives who will help lead Skydance, the soon-to-be merged Paramount Skydance and Warner Bros. Discovery , after the deal closes on Tuesday . The full leadership team brings together executives from both companies and will report to Ellison and Kreiz, according to a news release . Bari Weiss, editor-in-chief of CBS News, and Mark Thompson, chairman and editor-in-chief of CNN Worldwide, will remain in their roles and lead the company's news divisions after the merger is completed. Weiss joined Paramount Skydance in October 2025 when the company bought digital news outlet The Free Press, which she founded. Casey Bloys, currently chairman and CEO of HBO and Max content for WBD, will serve as co-chair and chief content officer of Skydance's direct-to-consumer division, overseeing the HBO Max and Paramount+ streaming businesses, while George Cheeks, formerly a co-CEO of Paramount, will serve as co-chair and chief content officer of Skydance TV, which includes the company's global sports group. JB Perrette, who most recently served as CEO and President of global streaming and games for Warner Bros. Discovery, will co-chair both divisions alongside Bloys and Cheeks. Paramount Chief Strategy Officer and Chief Operating Officer Andy Gordon will become president of Skydance. Chief Financial Officer Dennis Cinelli will stay in his role. "The leaders joining me have built some of the most beloved franchises and businesses in the industry, and they share a deep respect for the creative process and a belief that great stories have the power to entertain, unite and inspire audiences around the world," Ellison said in the release. Paramount Skydance and Warner Bros. Discovery announced the approximately $110 billion merger agreement in February. After settling a lawsuit from a group of state attorneys general last month, the companies announced last week that the deal would close on Tuesday.
